newsitem.title: LEBANON: Japanese officials see Red Army suspects in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Japanese officials see Red Army suspects in Beirut.

text.p: Japanese officials on Wednesday met suspected members of the Japanese Red Army detained in Beirut, Lebanon's Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum said.

The meetings, which took place at the Beirut law courts in the presence of Lebanese judicial authorities, were the first between Japanese officials and the suspects who were detained by Lebanon on February 15.
Addoum said the conversations between the eight Japanese in detention and the officials were restricted to personal matters and no discussion of the Japanese Red Army was permitted.
The Japanese officials asked the detainees if they wished to send messages to their families in Japan, but some of the detainees refused to give the officials their names, Addoum said.
The conversations were held in English with Lebanese officials listening, he said.
According to Addoum, Japan has provided documents identifying five of the suspects as Red Army guerrillas. Another three Japanese citizens and a Lebanese woman are also under arrest.
